item.title: Pentagon changes how it releases casualty data as Iran conflict continues
item.description: As U.S. service member deaths and injuries from Iranian attacks increased last week, the Pentagon shifted how it releases information on casualties.

item.title: Former Wisconsin Democratic chair says U.S. political system must change
item.description: Former chair of the Wisconsin Democratic Party, Ben Wikler, talks with NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer about his new book "This is the Plan: How to End America's Meltdown and Save Democracy."

item.title: 3 dead, 4 injured in shooting at Seattle food festival
item.description: One suspect is in custody following a mass shooting at a Seattle food festival on Sunday that left three victims dead and four others injured.
item.content:encoded: One suspect is in custody following a mass shooting at a Seattle food festival on Sunday that left three victims dead and four others injured.

item.description: The spat between the leading prediction market company and a key battleground state could be a glimpse into the next major fight between states and the fast-growing industry.

item.title: The quality of Iowa's water is spilling into the state's toss-up governor's race
item.description: In Iowa's competitive governor's race, farmers are raising longstanding concerns over water quality and agriculture's role in ultimately reducing the state's cancer rates.

item.title: Trump orders warning about 'inaccurate information' be placed outside D.C. museum
item.description: President Trump says Smithsonian exhibits are anti-white and dishonest. Museum leaders react to Trump's order that signage be placed outside a museum that "corrects inaccurate information."

item.title: With just a few primary elections to go, the competitive Senate map keeps shifting
item.description: For Democrats to take control of the U.S. Senate, they have to flip four seats currently held by Republicans. Republicans, meanwhile, are playing defense and pickup opportunities are harder to find.

item.title: Trump administration to announce rules for how states will share the Colorado River
item.description: This week the federal government is to release new rules for how much water each of the seven states that share the Colorado River will get. Effects on the ecosystem were largely left unconsidered.

item.title: Trump allies approve new rules that will weaken protections for historic sites
item.description: An advisory council stacked with President Trump's allies voted to relax a 60-year-old historic preservation law, paving the way for federal projects that could harm historic sites across the country.
